notes: Pool of 20 defects in five groups of four. Each attempt activates two per group (see scenarios/cedarvalley/attempt.js). Every defect is off by default, and the page with no defects active is intended to pass WCAG 2.2 Level A and AA.

violations.title: Date of birth format is not explained
violations.element: "Date of birth" field
violations.description: The date of birth field only accepts DD/MM/YYYY, but there is no hint saying so. Users must guess the format and recover from an error, which is especially hard for people with cognitive disabilities.
violations.how_to_find: Read the label and surrounding text for format instructions, then enter a date in another format (such as 1990-03-27) and submit.
violations.fix: Add a hint such as "Use the format DD/MM/YYYY, for example 27/03/1990" and link it with aria-describedby.

violations.title: Password requirements are not linked to the field
violations.element: "Password" field and its hint
violations.description: The hint "At least 10 characters, including at least one number" is visible above the field but not programmatically associated with it. Screen reader users who tab into the field hear only "Password, edit" and miss the rules.
violations.how_to_find: Tab to the password field with a screen reader and listen for the hint, or check the field's accessible description in the DevTools Accessibility pane.
violations.fix: Add the hint's id to the field's aria-describedby attribute.

violations.title: Two fields share the label "Name" (and two "Phone")
violations.element: Participant and Emergency contact name and phone fields
violations.description: The participant's and emergency contact's fields are both labelled just "Name" and "Phone". The sections are separated only by headings, so screen reader users moving between fields in forms mode cannot tell whose details each field wants.
violations.how_to_find: Tab through the form with a screen reader, or list the form fields (NVDA Insert+F7, VoiceOver rotor), and look for duplicate labels.
violations.fix: Use unique, descriptive labels ("Participant's full name", "Emergency contact's full name"), or group each section in a fieldset with a legend.

violations.title: Required fields are indicated only by red text
violations.element: Required field labels and the note at the top of the form
violations.description: The page says "Required fields are shown in red", and required labels are red with no other marker. Users who cannot perceive red cannot tell which fields are required, and screen readers do not convey the color.
violations.how_to_find: View the form in grayscale or with a color-blindness simulator. Listen to the labels with a screen reader.
violations.fix: Add "(required)" to required labels (and use the required or aria-required attribute), rather than relying on color.

violations.title: Missing program choice is shown only by color
violations.element: "Choose a program" radio group
violations.description: If no program is chosen, the group's legend turns red, but no error text appears and the error summary does not mention it. Users are not told in text what went wrong, and if it is the only error the form appears to do nothing.
violations.how_to_find: Fill in every field except the program and submit. Look for an error message about the program, and check whether a screen reader announces anything.
violations.fix: Show a text error ("Choose a program") in the group, link it with aria-describedby, and include it in the error summary.

violations.title: Format errors do not say how to fix them
violations.element: Error messages for date of birth, email and password
violations.description: When the date, email or password is in the wrong format, the message just says "Invalid date of birth.", "Invalid email address." or "Invalid password.". The required format is known but not given.
violations.how_to_find: Enter 1990-03-27 as the date of birth, "ana@" as the email and "short" as the password, then submit and read the messages.
violations.fix: Say what is needed, e.g. "Enter your date of birth as DD/MM/YYYY, for example 27/03/1990" and "Your password must be at least 10 characters and include a number".

violations.title: Error summary is not announced
violations.element: Error summary at the top of the form
violations.description: Submitting with errors displays an error summary at the top of the page, but focus stays on the Continue button at the bottom and the summary is not a live region. Screen reader users get no indication that the submission failed.
violations.how_to_find: Submit the empty form with a screen reader running. Note where focus is afterward and whether anything is announced.
violations.fix: Move focus to the error summary (tabindex="-1") after a failed submission, or give it role="alert".

violations.title: Inline error messages are not linked to their fields
violations.element: Inline error messages for every field
violations.description: Error messages appear above each invalid field, but the fields are not marked aria-invalid and the messages are not in their aria-describedby. Screen reader users tabbing to a field hear no error.
violations.how_to_find: Submit the empty form, then tab to a field with a screen reader and listen. Check the field's aria-invalid and accessible description in DevTools.
violations.fix: Set aria-invalid="true" on invalid fields and add each error message's id to its field's aria-describedby.

violations.title: Form fields have no visible focus indicator
violations.element: All inputs, radio buttons and checkboxes in the form
violations.description: The stylesheet removes the focus outline from form fields without replacing it. Keyboard users cannot see which field they are in.
violations.how_to_find: Tab through the form and watch for a focus indicator on each field. Inspect the :focus styles.
violations.fix: Restore a clearly visible focus style, e.g. a 3px outline with 3:1 contrast.

violations.title: Choosing a program moves focus unexpectedly
violations.element: "Choose a program" radio buttons
violations.description: Selecting a program immediately moves focus to the Equipment rental checkbox. Keyboard users who arrow through the options to compare them are thrown out of the group after the first arrow press.
violations.how_to_find: Tab into the program group and press the Down arrow. Note where focus goes.
violations.fix: Remove the change handler that moves focus, and let users move on with Tab.

violations.title: Terms checkbox cannot be used with the keyboard
violations.element: "I agree to the program terms" checkbox
violations.description: The terms checkbox is a styled span with a click handler. It cannot receive focus, has no checkbox role or checked state, and its label is not associated, so keyboard and screen reader users cannot agree to the terms and cannot register.
violations.how_to_find: Tab through the end of the form: focus skips the terms checkbox. Inspect it to see it is a span.
violations.fix: Use a native <input type="checkbox"> with an associated <label>.

violations.title: Form silently resets after 90 seconds of inactivity
violations.element: Whole registration form
violations.description: If the user stops typing for 90 seconds, everything entered is cleared without warning and with no way to extend the time. Users who type slowly, use switch access or step away to find information lose their work.
violations.how_to_find: Fill in a few fields, wait at least 90 seconds without touching the page, and check whether your entries are still there.
violations.fix: Remove the time limit, or warn users at least 20 seconds before it expires and let them extend it with a simple action.

violations.title: Billing address must be typed again
violations.element: Billing address section
violations.description: The billing address fields are always required, with no option to reuse the home address entered earlier in the same form. Users must re-enter information they have already provided.
violations.how_to_find: Complete the home address, then look at the billing address section for a way to reuse it.
violations.fix: Add a "Billing address is the same as my home address" checkbox (checked by default), or pre-fill the billing fields.

violations.title: Payment is taken with no chance to review
violations.element: "Register and pay" button
violations.description: Submitting a valid form immediately completes the registration and charges the fee. There is no review step, confirmation or way to correct mistakes before a financial commitment is made.
violations.how_to_find: Complete the form correctly and submit. Note whether you are shown your details to check before payment.
violations.fix: Add a review step that summarizes the registration and fee, with options to edit or confirm.

violations.title: Personal data fields do not identify their purpose
violations.element: Name, date of birth, email, phone, address and password fields
violations.description: None of the fields that collect the user's own information have autocomplete attributes. Browsers cannot autofill them, and tools that help people with cognitive disabilities cannot recognize the fields' purpose.
violations.how_to_find: Inspect the inputs for autocomplete attributes with valid tokens; try browser autofill.
violations.fix: Add the correct tokens: name, bday, email, tel, address-line1, address-level2, postal-code, the billing equivalents, and new-password.

violations.title: Show password toggle does not expose its state
violations.element: Password visibility toggle (eye icon)
violations.description: The icon button always has the name "Show password", even when the password is visible. Only the icon changes, so screen reader users cannot tell whether the password is shown.
violations.how_to_find: Activate the toggle with a screen reader and listen to its name and state before and after. Check for aria-pressed or a changing label in DevTools.
violations.fix: Change the accessible name to "Hide password" when the password is shown, or use aria-pressed to expose the toggle state.

violations.title: Hint text has insufficient contrast
violations.element: Field hints (date of birth and password)
violations.description: The hint text is light grey (#a6ada9) on white, about 2.3:1, below the 4.5:1 minimum. Low-vision users miss the format and password rules.
violations.how_to_find: Measure the hint text color against the background with a contrast analyzer. axe flags this as color-contrast.
violations.fix: Use a darker grey such as #5d6662 (about 5.9:1).

violations.title: Sticky fee bar hides focused fields
violations.element: Fixed "Total fee" bar at the bottom of the screen
violations.description: As keyboard users tab down the form, the next field is often already inside the viewport but under the fixed fee bar, so the browser does not scroll and the focused field is completely hidden.
violations.how_to_find: Tab slowly through the form at a typical window height and watch the bottom of the screen. Check for a field that is focused but entirely covered by the bar.
violations.fix: Add scroll-padding-bottom (at least the bar's height) to the html element so focused fields scroll clear of the bar.

violations.title: Instructions rely on color and location
violations.element: Instruction at the top of the form
violations.description: The instruction says "press the green button at the bottom right of the screen". Screen reader users and people who cannot perceive green cannot identify the button from that description.
violations.how_to_find: Read the instructional text and check whether it identifies the control only by color or position.
violations.fix: Refer to the button by its label: "When you have finished, select Continue to review."

violations.title: Checkbox and radio borders are too faint
violations.element: Program radio buttons and add-on checkboxes
violations.description: The custom-styled radio buttons and checkboxes have a #dde1df border on white, about 1.3:1. Low-vision users cannot see the controls until they are checked.
violations.how_to_find: Measure the unchecked control borders against the background with a contrast analyzer.
violations.fix: Use a border with at least 3:1 contrast, such as #5d6662, or keep the native controls.
